title: ephemeral-gpu-contention-silent-degradation-investigation-notes
body:
Overview:

Quick notes from the last three on‑call windows where we observed small, hard‑to‑pinpoint performance degradations on Dedicated GPU pools: not a full outage, but a 10–25% drop in tokens/sec for a subset of tenants while latency p50/p90 stayed mostly stable and p99 crept up. These incidents tend to self‑recover or respond to pool rebalancing, which makes them easy to miss in automated postmortems. This file collects signals, short remediation steps, and hypotheses to turn into a concrete runbook.

Why this matters:
- Customer impact is subtle but measurable for inference workloads with tight cost/latency SLAs (batching-sensitive jobs, streaming chat).
- Noisy tenant symptoms are not always 'noisy' (high GPU util) — sometimes the workload causes micro contention (memory allocation cost, kernel launch jitter, PCIe bus bursts) that reduces throughput without clear saturation signals.
- We need deterministic detection and safe, fast mitigations for oncall.

Observed signal set (ordered by usefulness):
1) Inference tokens/sec drop correlated with increased kernel_launch_time_ms (DL kernels) and increased scheduler_queue_length on allocator.
2) NVLINK/PCIe error or retry counters spike in 10–90s windows (DCGM metrics).
3) Per-tenant average GPU memory fragmentation metric (approx from DRAM allocator churn) increases prior to throughput drop.
4) GPUUtil stays medium/high but SM_efficiency and achieved_occupancy drop — suggests poor kernel concurrency, not raw compute shortage.
5) KV cache hit rate drops for affected tenants (indicates eviction patterns or cache amplification).
6) Autoscaler triggers small scale-ups that do not restore tokens/sec immediately (indicates placement-level contention).

Immediate (oncall) checklist — quick triage and mitigation:
- Step 0: Confirm scope via Grafana dashboard (dedicated/pool/*): tokens/sec, kernel_launch_time_ms, DCGM ECC/PCIe counters, per-tenant request rates.
- Step 1: If degradation < 10 minutes and self‑recovering, annotate incident, run targeted sampling (see below) and watch for recurrence.
- Step 2: If tokens/sec drop > 15% and customer complaints incoming, attempt soft isolation: apply allocation_tag = "isolate-temp" to the suspected tenant (via allocator admin API) to land them on a different pool node. This is reversible and faster than full rollback.
- Step 3: If soft isolation risky or not possible, trigger temporary per-tenant throttling (quota down to 60% for 3–5m) to reduce bursty allocation churn.
- Step 4: If pool-level signals show NVLINK/PCIe retries or driver errors, cordon node(s) and migrate in-flight low‑priority jobs off the node (use eviction window).
- Step 5: If eviction/migration required, prefer draining nodes with abnormal kernel_launch_time_ms over nodes with higher raw GPUUtil.

Data collection commands (useful oncall snippets):
- nvidia-smi dmon -s uct -d 2 > /tmp/dmon.log (short run)
- dcgmi diag --get-status; dcgm_exporter metrics snapshot
- eBPF trace (lightweight): trace kernel_launch syscall latencies for the tenant container cgroup (proto script in /ops/ebpf/launch-latency.sh)
- allocator debug API: GET /admin/pools/<pool>/allocations?filter=tenant:<id>&fields=alloc_time,eviction_count,placement_node
- capture perf counters: nvprof-like lightweight capture if safe (coord with infra)

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Memory allocator fragmentation: some workloads frequently allocate/deallocate many small tensors; fragmentation increases kernel readiness time and GC pauses. Explains memory‑fragmentation metric and KV cache churn.
B) PCIe/NVLINK microbursts: inter-GPU communication spikes causing short stalls that reduce achieved occupancy but don't drive high util or temperature. Matches PCIe retry spikes.
C) Driver/firmware scheduling jitter: occasional driver pathologies when combined with certain CUDA kernels; results in increased kernel launch latency and scheduling queueing.
D) Allocator placement hot‑spotting: autoscaler or allocator placed many tenants on same NUMA/PCIe topology causing intra-node contention (not captured by raw GPUUtil).

Hypothesis tests to run (post‑incident):
- Recreate offline with the same batch pattern and small allocations; measure fragmentation and kernel_launch_time.
- Replay network/PCIe load in a staging cluster to check NVLINK retry thresholds.
- Run controlled allocations that force crossing of memory pages to see eviction/churn amplification.

Short-term engineering work (owner & ETA proposals):
- Add kernel_launch_time_ms to pool health alerting (owner: Priya, ETA 2w).
- Expose per‑tenant memory churn and page_fault_count via allocator debug API (owner: Diego, ETA 3w).
- Patch allocator to support "soft isolation" tags that automatically shift noisy tenants after X degradation events (owner: Liam, ETA 4w).

Long-term mitigations and product changes:
- Introduce a low‑latency placement policy for streaming chat workloads (pinning + pre-warmed KV caches) to avoid dynamic placement churn.
- Implement microburst shaping: budget per-tenant for NVLINK/PCIe bandwidth over sliding windows.
- Better telemetry: correlate DCGM bus counters with per-tenant traces in Flamegraphs and a heatmap UI.

Playbook draft for final runbook (to be cleaned and codified in Confluence):
1) Detection triggers: sustained tokens/sec drop > 15% for 5m + kernel_launch_time_ms > baseline*1.5.
2) Initial automated action: mark tenant as candidate noisy; if two candidate noisy events in 1h, auto-apply "isolate-temp" tag and alert SRE.
3) Automated graceful degradation: reduce tenant burst concurrency by 30% for 10m; if no improvement, escalate to manual isolation.
4) Node cordon criteria: NVLINK/PCIe retries > X for 2m OR kernel_launch_time_ms abnormal on >2 containers on same node.
5) Postmortem template entries: timeline, metrics snapshot, sampling artifacts (dmon, allocator logs, eBPF traces), action taken, time to recovery, customer impact estimate.

Open questions / notes to self:
- What exact DCGM metric threshold reasonably separates benign retries vs contention? Need historical baseline from last 6 months.
- Can we cheaply instrument kernel launch latency without heavy eBPF overhead in prod? Need perf cost numbers.
- How will soft isolation interact with Dedicated reserved capacity billing? Product needs signoff.

Immediate next steps (actionable):
- Priya: add kernel_launch_time_ms panel on dedicated-pool health dashboard by EOW.
- Diego: add allocator API field for eviction_count and recent_alloc_latency by next sprint.
- Liam: prototype soft-isolation workflow (admin API -> tag -> rebalancer) and demo in staging next week.
- Asha (me): run retrospective with infra and product next Tue to decide billing/product impact.

Appendix: quick incident examples (shortened)
- Incident A (2025-01-18 03:12 UTC): Podset A on pool eu-west experienced 18% tokens/sec drop for 23m. kernel_launch_time increased from 1.2ms -> 4.6ms. NVLINK retries spiked twice. Soft isolation moved tenant to another node; recovery in 4m. No customer-facing outage.
- Incident B (2025-01-29 19:40 UTC): Intermittent p99 spikes; allocator reported increased eviction_count correlated with a new tenant rollout. After per-tenant throttling, perf returned to baseline.

Notes on writing style here: intentionally informal — this is a working doc. Will convert into a formal runbook once we validate hypotheses and implement the required telemetry.

-- end --
